enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1054 AM MST Sun Nov 15 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 1013 AM MST Sun Nov 15 2026

 - A back door cold front will push through the region tonight and
   bring cooler temperatures to eastern areas along with some
   breezy conditions over the lowlands for Monday.

 - A chance of rain showers for western New Mexico on Tuesday
   night as a storm system crosses the Central Rockies. 
   
 - Temperatures warm a bit later in the week, with lowland highs 
   in the upper 60s/lower 70s. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1013 AM MST Sun Nov 15 2026

Currently an upper low sits over SW OK with a ridge building in
from the west. There is a back door cold front pushing through SE
NM and will make it into far eastern areas by sunset. This isn't a
real strong front, but winds will pick up to 10-20mph on western
mountain slopes. Low clouds and some patchy fog can be expected,
especially along the eastern slopes of the Sacs and into parts of
Hudspeth county. May see some patchy lower clouds as far west as
El Paso. The easterly winds will push through the remainder of the
area overnight and start to increase out on the Lordsburg Playa by
morning. Tomorrow will see cooler temperatures by 5-10 degrees
east and similar to today than out west. Did lower NBM temps out
east where it typically has a warm bias behind these fronts and
with some lingering lower clouds possible. 

Going into Monday night and Tuesday, there will be an upper trough
moving into CA and increasing southwest flow aloft. The low level
winds will gradually turn more southerly and tap some moisture,
but as the trough lifts northeast into Tue night and early Wed,
the best lift will remain north of the CWA, but do expect some
light rain showers in the Gila region and maybe some spill over
into the Sacs. The warm SW flow aloft will keep precip type all
rain except some of the highest peaks. NBM may be a little high
with PoPs in the far NW CWA with 60s, but think sometime Tue night
there will be a few hundredths most areas.  

West-southwest flow continues into next weekend with temperatures
warming up to about 5-10 degrees above normal through Thu then a
weak Pacific cold front moves through Fri into Sat. May bet a
little breezy Fri but looks like best lift again remains north and
little to no precip chances.  

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1013 AM MST Sun Nov 15 2026

P6SM FEW050-070 FEW-SCT250 through most off the area except there
will be some low clouds moving in behind a back door cold front
into eastern areas. There will be areas of BKN010-020 moving into
the eastern Sacramento Mountains by 21Z and pushing SW through the
evening. Some FEW-SCT020-030 possible on eastern mountain slopes
up to KELP by morning. Winds will be AOB 10KTS through the
afternoon but will be shifting to the E to SE at 5-15KTS through
the overnight from east to west and continuing through 18Z. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1013 AM MST Sun Nov 15 2026

Little fire concern through the upcoming week. A back door cold
front pushes through tonight and will drop temps in eastern areas
for early in the work week with occasional low end breezy
conditions on the NM lowlands. An upper trough will bring some
light rain showers to the Gila region and possibly the Sacs for
Tue night but overall rainfall amounts will be on the light side. 
Temperatures warm back up for the end of the week but RH's remain
above 25-30% areawide. Winds will become breezy again Friday. Vent
rates Mon will be poor to fair and improve to fair to good Tue.
